title: Key-value store
intro: You are writing a tiny in-memory key-value store, one class `Store` that grows level by level. Use only the standard library. Time is passed in explicitly (`now`, in seconds) so your code is easy to test; it defaults to 0.
rules: Keys are strings and values can be anything. A missing (or expired) key reads as None.
Keep every method O(1) on average, except where a level says otherwise.

levels.title: get/set/delete
levels.prompt: Write `Store` with `set(key, value)`, `get(key)` (the value, or None when the key is missing) and `delete(key)` (True if the key existed and was removed, False otherwise). Setting an existing key replaces its value.
levels.signature:
class Store:
    def set(self, key: str, value) -> None: ...
    def get(self, key: str): ...
    def delete(self, key: str) -> bool: ...
levels.sampleInput:
s = Store()
s.set("a", 1)
s.set("b", 2)
s.set("a", 3)
print(s.get("a"), s.get("b"), s.get("z"))
print(s.delete("b"), s.delete("b"))
print(s.get("b"))
edgeCases: Deleting a missing key returns False and changes nothing
A stored None value and a missing key both read as None; that is fine here

levels.title: Keys with TTL
levels.prompt: Extend `Store` so `set(key, value, ttl=None, now=0)` can give a key a time-to-live in seconds: the key expires at `now + ttl` and is gone when `current_time >= now + ttl`. `get(key, now=0)` and `delete(key, now=0)` take the current time and treat an expired key as missing (`delete` returns False for it). A `set` replaces any earlier TTL; without `ttl` the key never expires.
levels.signature:
class Store:
    def set(self, key: str, value, ttl: int | None = None, now: int = 0) -> None: ...
    def get(self, key: str, now: int = 0): ...
    def delete(self, key: str, now: int = 0) -> bool: ...
levels.sampleInput:
s = Store()
s.set("a", 1, ttl=10, now=0)
print(s.get("a", now=5), s.get("a", now=10))
s.set("b", 2)
print(s.get("b", now=100))
s.set("a", 5, ttl=5, now=20)
print(s.get("a", now=24), s.get("a", now=25))
print(s.delete("a", now=30))
edgeCases: At exactly now + ttl the key is already expired
Expire lazily on read: you do not need a background cleaner

levels.title: begin/rollback/commit transactions
levels.prompt: Add transactions that can be nested. `begin()` opens a transaction. Inside it, `set` and `delete` work as before but can be undone. `rollback()` undoes every change made since the matching `begin()` and returns True (False if no transaction is open). `commit()` closes the innermost transaction and keeps its changes, returning True (False if none is open); if it was nested, the parent transaction can still roll those changes back. Track changes with a stack: for each open transaction remember the previous value of every key it touched.
levels.signature:
class Store:
    def begin(self) -> None: ...
    def rollback(self) -> bool: ...
    def commit(self) -> bool: ...
levels.sampleInput:
s = Store()
s.set("a", 1)
s.begin()
s.set("a", 2)
s.set("b", 3)
print(s.get("a"), s.get("b"))
s.begin()
s.delete("a")
print(s.get("a"))
print(s.rollback())
print(s.get("a"))
print(s.commit())
print(s.get("a"), s.get("b"))
print(s.rollback())
s.begin()
s.set("b", 9)
print(s.rollback(), s.get("b"))
edgeCases: Rolling back a key that did not exist before the transaction removes it again
Remember only the FIRST old value of a key within one transaction
